atAGlance: Bánh xèo is a crisp turmeric-rice pancake eaten by tearing pieces into rice paper or lettuce with herbs, then dipping in the fish-sauce dip.
whatItIs: Bánh xèo is a sizzling turmeric-rice pancake folded around pork, shrimp, bean sprouts, and herbs. The local fun is not fork-and-knife pancake eating: you tear it, wrap it with rice paper or lettuce and herbs, then dip in the fish-sauce dip.
howToEnjoy: Tear off a crisp piece, tuck it into rice paper or lettuce with herbs, roll or fold it, then dip lightly in the fish-sauce dip. The herbs and wrapper are part of the dish, not decoration.
howLocalsOrder: Order bánh xèo expecting a hands-on wrap-and-dip plate. Ask for extra rice paper or herbs if the table is sharing, and say no chili in the fish-sauce dip before dipping starts.
worthKnowing: Bánh xèo changes by region, but the eating ritual is the traveler key: crisp pancake, fresh herbs, rice paper or lettuce, and bright fish-sauce dip in one bite.
goodToKnow: Fresh herbs are part of the flavor, not a garnish. Skip chili if you want the fish-sauce dip milder.
